note: URL-friendly Options has no config, no configure route, no permissions, no Drush, no plugins. It alters field_config_edit_form for options-list fields: adds an #element_validate that rejects allowed-values keys not matching ^[a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+$, and overrides the machine-name element to use hyphens. hook_requirements() (runtime) flags existing list_string field storages with non-compliant keys. hook_url_friendly_options_bypass_field_validation($field_name,$entity_type_id) exempts a field. It never rewrites existing values. Medium/hard cases create namespaced list_string fields (field_ufo_*) on node.article (programmatic creation bypasses the form validation) and read/assert their allowed_values keys against the module's URL-friendly rule.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal url_friendly_options module enforce on option-list (select/list) fields, and what characters are allowed in the option keys?
evals.expected_output: It enforces that option-list field keys (allowed_values keys) are URL-friendly: only alphanumeric characters and hyphens (regex ^[a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+$), so they work as clean URL segments / Views contextual-filter arguments. It also makes the machine-name helper suggest hyphens instead of underscores.

evals.prompt: A developer needs one specific field to be exempt from url_friendly_options validation. Which hook do they implement, and what should it return?
evals.expected_output: Implement hook_url_friendly_options_bypass_field_validation($field_name, $entity_type_id) and return TRUE for the field to exempt (FALSE otherwise). It bypasses both the field-form validation and the status-report requirements check.

evals.prompt: If I enable url_friendly_options on a site that already has option-list fields with underscore keys, does it rewrite the existing keys? How would I find out which fields are non-compliant?
evals.expected_output: No - it never changes existing stored values. It blocks adding/editing values while non-compliant keys exist (the field form won't validate), and its hook_requirements() adds a status-report error at /admin/reports/status listing the entity_type.field_name of any list_string storage with non-URL-friendly keys.

evals.prompt: This site has an option-list field named field_ufo_known on the Article content type. Inspect its live allowed-values and identify which option key is NOT URL-friendly according to url_friendly_options' rules.
evals.expected_output: The key 'bad_key' is not URL-friendly (underscore is not allowed). field.storage.node.field_ufo_known allowed_values has keys bad_key and good-key; only bad_key fails the ^[a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+$ rule.

evals.prompt: The Article content type on this site has two option-list fields, field_ufo_ok and field_ufo_bad. Inspect their live allowed-values and state which field would fail url_friendly_options' URL-friendly key check.
evals.expected_output: field_ufo_bad fails: its allowed_values include the key 'light_grey' (underscore), which is not URL-friendly. field_ufo_ok uses red and dark-blue, which are both valid.

evals.prompt: On this site, add an option-list (list_string) field named field_ufo_task to the Article content type with at least two allowed values, choosing option keys that satisfy url_friendly_options (URL-friendly: only letters, numbers and hyphens). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a list_string field storage field_ufo_task on node with allowed_values whose keys are all URL-friendly (e.g. ['first-value' => 'First value', 'second-value' => 'Second value']) and a FieldConfig on article. Every key must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+$ and there must be >= 2 options.

evals.prompt: The Article content type has an option-list field field_ufo_fix whose allowed-values keys currently use underscores (bad_key_1, bad_key_2) and therefore violate url_friendly_options. Rename the option keys so they are URL-friendly (letters, numbers and hyphens only), keeping the two options, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Update field.storage.node.field_ufo_fix allowed_values so both keys are URL-friendly, e.g. ['bad-key-1' => 'First', 'bad-key-2' => 'Second'] (or 'first'/'second'). Every key must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+$ and there must still be >= 2 options.
